rationale: Neuroimaging characterization from the defining international cohort study (Kaiyrzhanov et al., 2024; 45 patients across 28 families) confirms that ACBD6 deficiency features a selective focal midline neuroimaging pattern rather than diffuse pontocerebellar hypoplasia (PCH). Specifically, posterior fossa and brainstem anomalies manifest as a short midbrain (38%, n=11) and a small inferior cerebellar vermis (38%, n=11), frequently accompanied by clava hypertrophy (24%), corpus callosum abnormalities (70%), and anterior commissure hypoplasia/agenesis (66%). This pattern stands in stark contrast to classical PCH disorders, which are characterized by diffuse pontine flattening, dragonfly-like cerebellar hemisphere atrophy, and broad infratentorial hypoplasia.

evidence.text: In 45 individuals with bi-allelic ACBD6 pathogenic variants, midline brain malformations showed a distinct focal distribution: corpus callosum abnormalities occurred in 70%, hypoplasia or agenesis of the anterior commissure in 66%, short midbrain in 38%, small inferior cerebellar vermis in 38%, and clava hypertrophy in 24%.

source.title: Bi-allelic ACBD6 variants lead to a neurodevelopmental syndrome with progressive and complex movement disorders
source.quote: Midline brain malformations including corpus callosum abnormalities (70%), hypoplasia/agenesis of the anterior commissure (66%), short midbrain and small inferior cerebellar vermis (38% each) as well as hypertrophy of the clava (24%) were common neuroimaging findings.

evidence.text: Detailed morphological evaluation of brain MRIs in the ACBD6 cohort showed short midbrain and small inferior cerebellar vermis in 11 patients each, confirming a localized inferior vermian and midbrain involvement.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true clinical sensitivity of anterior commissure hypoplasia combined with clava hypertrophy versus isolated inferior vermian hypoplasia for differentiating ACBD6 deficiency from PCH2 and PCH1?
new_directions.rationale: Because short midbrain and inferior vermian hypoplasia are each detected in only 38% of patients, their absence does not exclude ACBD6 deficiency. Determining the diagnostic sensitivity and specificity of the full midline neuroimaging composite (anterior commissure + corpus callosum + clava + vermis) across differential mimic cohorts is needed.
